newsitem.title: SPAIN: Opera says low bid could win Spain's Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Opera says low bid could win Spain's Retevision.

text.p: The Opera Group, a consortium bidding for Spain's Retevision and a second license to operate basic telephone services, said on Wednesday its offer could win, despite having been outbid financially by another group.
"We are convinced that as a whole our offer represents the ideal option for...Retevision," Opera director Nicolas Merigo told journalists.
He said the decision would be based not only on the financial offer, but also on other factors like infrastructure and future benefit to the Spanish economy.

Opera, made of Spanish bank BCH, France Telecom and U.S. operator Sprint, presented an offer of 130 billion pesetas for 70 percent Retevision's capital against the 180 billion pesetas bid by the group led by Spanish electricity firm Endesa and Italy's Stet.
The Endesa/Stet offer gets 400 out 1,000 points because it is the highest bid, but Merigo said his project would get the remaining points.

The government, which is selling the stake in state broadcaster Retevision along with the license to compete in basic services with Telefonica de Espana, will give 40 percent weight to the highest bid.
But it will also weigh infrastructure (20 percent), financing (20 percent), experience (10 percent) and benefit for Spanish companies (10 percent).
Merigo said Opera had the better infrastructure thanks to a deal with state railway Renfe, which will be cheaper and easier to expand than the electricity networks of Endesa.

Analysts had said they favoured the Endesa bid because of the electricity utility's extensive networks, as well as its predominantly Spanish participation with Union Fenosa, Basque telephone operator Euskatel and some small Spanish banks backing it.

The Opera director said Retevision would have pre-tax, writedown and interest payment profit from the start due to its existing audiovisual business and net profit and positive cash flow after the years 2000 and 2002 respectively.
The government has two months from the bid presentation last week to make a decision, but Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado has said the winner will be known by the end of June.
